Panel A of @afnan2023ValidatingMEGSource Figure 2: group average of relative
PSD per frequency band, per 38-region iEEG atlas ROI, shown side-by-side for
ground-truth iEEG and the MEG-estimated ViEEG. Here we substitute HD-EEG
source-reconstructed signals for the MEG ViEEG. Within each band, iEEG and
the reconstructed modality share a color scale so the maps are directly
comparable; the scale changes between bands.

```{python}
#| label: imports
from pathlib import Path
from IPython.display import Markdown
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import scipy.stats as stats
from plotnine import (
    aes,
    element_text,
    ggplot,
    labs,
    scale_fill_cmap,
    theme,
    theme_void,
)

from ggsegpy.geom_brain import geom_brain

from pesco.atlases import load_frauscher
from pesco.io import load_sources, prepare_psd
from pesco.preprocess import compute_psd, normalize_psd

PROJECT_DIR = Path("/Users/daniel/PhD/spectral-comparison/code/")
DATA_PATH_IEEG = PROJECT_DIR / "data/Frauscher2018"
DATA_PATH_SOURCES = PROJECT_DIR / "data/Mantini2018"

# HD-EEG source data was high-pass filtered at 1 Hz; align iEEG to the same
# lower bound so per-channel "total power" is computed over the same range
# and the two modalities are comparable.
FREQ_RANGE = (1.0, 80.0)
# Canonical chapter bands (ch02_2_methods): 1 Hz lower bound throughout, gamma
# split at 45 Hz into lower/higher to separate residual line-noise from genuine HFA.
BANDS = [
    ("δ", 1.0, 4.0),
    ("θ", 4.0, 8.0),
    ("α", 8.0, 13.0),
    ("β", 13.0, 30.0),
    ("lower γ", 30.0, 45.0),
    ("higher γ", 45.0, 80.0),
]
BAND_ORDER = [b[0] for b in BANDS]

fig_dir = Path("figures")
fig_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
```

## Load both modalities

```{python}
#| label: load-ieeg
#| output: false
# iEEG: normalize=False → keep raw V²/Hz; we normalise to unit-integral below
# so the integration logic is shared with the HD modality.
ieeg_f, ieeg_psd_df = prepare_psd(
    matfile=DATA_PATH_IEEG / "WakefulnessMatlabFile.mat",
    region_dict_file=DATA_PATH_IEEG / "RegionInformation.csv",
    frauscher_bandpass=False,
    normalize=False,
    freq_range=FREQ_RANGE,
)
ieeg_psd_df.head()
#Markdown(ieeg_psd_df.head().round(2).to_markdown(index=False))
```

```{python}
#| label: load-hd
#| output: false

hd_raw, hd_meta = load_sources(DATA_PATH_SOURCES)
hd_f, hd_psd = compute_psd(
    hd_raw.get_data(), hd_raw.info["sfreq"], fmin=FREQ_RANGE[0], fmax=FREQ_RANGE[1]
)
assert np.isclose(ieeg_f[0], hd_f[0]) and np.isclose(ieeg_f[-1], hd_f[-1]), (
    "iEEG and HD frequency grids must align for relative PSD comparability"
)
hd_psd_df = pd.DataFrame(
    hd_psd, index=pd.Index(hd_raw.ch_names, name="ch_name"), columns=hd_f
).join(hd_meta)
hd_psd_df.head()
#Markdown(hd_psd_df.head().round(2).to_markdown(index=False))
```

## Per-channel band-relative power

Following @afnan2023ValidatingMEGSource sec. 2.9: per channel, relative PSD
bin = `PSD(f) / Σ_f PSD(f)` (each value divided by total power across the
whole frequency range; bins sum to 1). The per-band value is the **sum** of
those relative-PSD bins across the band — equivalently the fraction of
total power in the band, in [0, 1]. This matches the paper's reported
scales (anterior δ ≈ 0.36 = 36 % of total power in delta).

The paper's prose "group average across all channels within a ROI and all
frequency bins in each band" describes per-ROI averaging over channels of
the per-channel band sum; "across all frequency bins" reads as the
within-band aggregation, which must be a sum for the displayed scale to
range up to 0.36 in δ (a mean across 7 bins would top out near 0.05).

```{python}
#| label: band-rel-power
def band_relative_power(
    psd_df: pd.DataFrame, freqs: np.ndarray, region_col: str
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-channel fraction of total power in each canonical band."""
    freqs = np.asarray(freqs, dtype=float)
    psd = psd_df[list(freqs)].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    rel = psd / psd.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True)    # bare ratio, sums to 1

    out = {}
    last_name = BANDS[-1][0]
    for name, lo, hi in BANDS:
        mask = (freqs >= lo) & (freqs <= hi if name == last_name else freqs < hi)
        out[name] = rel[:, mask].sum(axis=1)       # ∈ [0, 1]

    band_df = pd.DataFrame(out, index=psd_df.index)
    band_df[region_col] = psd_df[region_col].to_numpy()
    return band_df


ieeg_bands = band_relative_power(ieeg_psd_df, ieeg_f, region_col="ChannelRegion")
hd_bands = band_relative_power(hd_psd_df, hd_f, region_col="region_number")
ieeg_bands.head()
```

```{python}
#| label: roi-mean
# Group average per ROI (frauscher_id 1-38). Bilateral ROIs collapse —
# Afnan averages over all channels in a ROI regardless of hemisphere.
ieeg_roi = (
    ieeg_bands.groupby("ChannelRegion")[BAND_ORDER]
    .mean()
    .rename_axis("frauscher_id")
    .reset_index()
)
hd_roi = (
    hd_bands.groupby("region_number")[BAND_ORDER]
    .mean()
    .rename_axis("frauscher_id")
    .reset_index()
)
ieeg_roi.head()
```

## Map ROI values onto the Frauscher 38-region atlas

```{python}
#| label: atlas
atlas = load_frauscher()
core = atlas.core[["label", "frauscher_id", "region", "hemi"]]


def roi_to_labels(roi_df: pd.DataFrame, modality: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Long: one row per (atlas label, band) with the ROI mean attached."""
    merged = core.merge(roi_df, on="frauscher_id", how="left")
    long = merged.melt(
        id_vars=["label", "frauscher_id", "region", "hemi"],
        value_vars=BAND_ORDER,
        var_name="band",
        value_name="value",
    )
    long["modality"] = modality
    return long


ieeg_long = roi_to_labels(ieeg_roi, "iEEG")
hd_long = roi_to_labels(hd_roi, "HD-EEG source")
plot_df = pd.concat([ieeg_long, hd_long], ignore_index=True)
plot_df["band"] = pd.Categorical(plot_df["band"], categories=BAND_ORDER, ordered=True)

# Welch's t-test per ROI and band
t_stat_rows = []
for r in range(1, 39):
    for name, lo, hi in BANDS:
        ieeg_vals = ieeg_bands.loc[ieeg_bands["ChannelRegion"] == r, name].to_numpy()
        hd_vals = hd_bands.loc[hd_bands["region_number"] == r, name].to_numpy()
        t_val, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(
            ieeg_vals, hd_vals, equal_var=False, nan_policy="omit"
        )
        alpha_corrected = 0.05 / (38 * len(BANDS))
        is_significant = p_val < alpha_corrected
        t_stat_rows.append({
            "frauscher_id": r,
            "band": name,
            "t_stat": t_val if is_significant else np.nan,
            "p_val": p_val,
            "is_significant": is_significant
        })
t_df = pd.DataFrame(t_stat_rows)

def t_to_labels(t_df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    merged = core.merge(t_df, on="frauscher_id", how="left")
    merged = merged.rename(columns={"t_stat": "value"})
    merged["modality"] = "t_map"
    return merged[["label", "band", "value", "modality"]]

t_long = t_to_labels(t_df)
```

## Figure 2A — relative PSD on the cortical surface

Per paper §2.9 / Fig. 2 caption: "color bar ranges from minimum to maximum
value among iEEG and ViEEG in each frequency band, such that the scale is
the same for both modalities in a given band". Each band gets its own
color scale spanning that band's joint iEEG + HD range; values plotted
in their native [0, 1] units (no global rescaling). Composed via plotnine
0.15 native `|` / `/` operators so each row keeps its own fill scale.

```{python}
from functools import reduce
from operator import truediv

# Colorscale for relative PSD. Try: "viridis", "magma", "plasma", "Spectral_r", or "jet"
PSD_COLORSCALE = "viridis"

def band_row(
    name: str,
    lo: float,
    hi: float,
    show_title: bool = True,
    title_ieeg: str = None,
    title_hd: str = None,
    title_t: str = None,
):
    sub = plot_df.loc[plot_df["band"] == name, ["label", "modality", "value"]]
    vmin = float(sub["value"].min())
    vmax = float(sub["value"].max())
    scale = scale_fill_cmap(
        cmap_name=PSD_COLORSCALE,
        limits=(vmin, vmax),
        name="Relative PSD",
    )

    def panel(modality: str, title: str | None, show_legend: bool):
        d = sub.loc[sub["modality"] == modality, ["label", "value"]]
        p = (
            ggplot(d, aes(fill="value"))
            + geom_brain(
                atlas=atlas, mapping=aes(fill="value"), hemi="left", show_legend=show_legend
            )
            + scale
            + theme_void()
            + theme(
                plot_title=element_text(size=9, weight="bold", family="sans-serif"),
                legend_position="right" if show_legend else "none",
                legend_direction="vertical",
                legend_title=element_text(size=8, weight="bold", family="sans-serif"),
                legend_text=element_text(size=7, family="sans-serif"),
                legend_key_height=40,
                legend_key_width=6,
                legend_box_spacing=0.04,
            )
        )
        if title is not None:
            p = p + labs(title=title)
        return p

    sub_t = t_long.loc[t_long["band"] == name, ["label", "value"]]
    scale_t = scale_fill_cmap(
        cmap_name="RdBu_r",
        limits=(-15, 15),
        na_value="lightgray",
        name="t-statistic",
    )

    def panel_t(title: str | None, show_legend: bool):
        p = (
            ggplot(sub_t, aes(fill="value"))
            + geom_brain(
                atlas=atlas, mapping=aes(fill="value"), hemi="left", show_legend=show_legend
            )
            + scale_t
            + theme_void()
            + theme(
                plot_title=element_text(size=9, weight="bold", family="sans-serif"),
                legend_position="right" if show_legend else "none",
                legend_direction="vertical",
                legend_title=element_text(size=8, weight="bold", family="sans-serif"),
                legend_text=element_text(size=7, family="sans-serif"),
                legend_key_height=40,
                legend_key_width=6,
                legend_box_spacing=0.04,
            )
        )
        if title is not None:
            p = p + labs(title=title)
        return p

    t_ieeg = title_ieeg if title_ieeg is not None else (f"{name} ({lo:g}-{hi:g} Hz)  iEEG" if show_title else f"{name} ({lo:g}-{hi:g} Hz)")
    t_hd = title_hd if title_hd is not None else ("ViEEG" if show_title else None)
    t_t = title_t if title_t is not None else ("Welch t-map" if show_title else None)

    left = panel("iEEG", t_ieeg, show_legend=False) + theme(plot_title=element_text(hjust=-0.15))
    right = panel("HD-EEG source", t_hd, show_legend=True)
    middle_t = panel_t(t_t, show_legend=True)
    return left | right | middle_t
```

```{python}
p = band_row("δ", 1.0, 4.0)
p
```


```{python}
#| label: fig-2a
#| fig-cap: "Group average relative PSD per ROI for the iEEG atlas (left) and HD-EEG source-reconstructed signals (right). One row per canonical band; within a row the two modalities share a color scale spanning that band's joint min-max Hippocampus and amygdala have no cortical-surface geometry in the Frauscher ggsegpy atlas and are not shown."



def build_fig():
    rows = [band_row(n, lo, hi, show_title=(i == 0)) for i, (n, lo, hi) in enumerate(BANDS)]
    return reduce(truediv, rows)

# plotnine.composition mutates internal layout state on save → rebuild per export.
build_fig().save(fig_dir / "fig2a_relative_psd.pdf", width=14, height=15, verbose=False)
build_fig().save(fig_dir / "fig2a_relative_psd.svg", width=14, height=15, verbose=False)
build_fig().save(
    fig_dir / "fig2a_relative_psd.png", width=14, height=15, dpi=150, verbose=False
)
build_fig()
```

## Notes

- Hippocampus (r37) and amygdala (r38) are present in the Frauscher 38-ROI
  iEEG atlas but lack 2D cortical-surface geometry in the bundled ggsegpy
  atlas; `geom_brain` warns and skips them.
- The paper's panel B (t-statistic map, Bonferroni-corrected per ROI × band)
  is omitted here; reuse the same `plot_df` skeleton with a Welch t-test per
  ROI to add it.
